evidence_note: NEMA described the Kogi flood situation as devastating and advised floodplain residents to relocate.
Houses in Yenagoa were reported submerged after two days of torrential rain.
Vice President flood assessment reported visibly rising flood conditions including Onitsha.
Sentinel-2 imagery showed flooded crop areas along the Hadejia River on 22 September 2018.
Benue water-resources commissioner assessed the active Makurdi flood; Wurukum and other areas were reported submerged after the overnight downpour.
Flooding after a downpour and Hadejia-Jamaare River overflow affected Hadejia LGA among four Jigawa LGAs and displaced hundreds of families.
Persistent downpour and rising River Niger submerged houses along the river bank in Lokoja; three buildings were reported submerged and occupants evacuated.
A report documents active flood conditions at Epie Creek in Agudama-Epie within Yenagoa LGA and residents crossing the flooded creek by boat.
An all-night heavy rain submerged Wurukum Market Wadata Market Vandeikya Street and NKST Church Low Level in Makurdi and displaced residents.
A contemporaneous report documented ravaging floodwater around the Ochanja Market roundabout axis in Onitsha following heavy downpour.
A Jigawa government and SEMA flood assessment team visited flood victims at Ganuwar Kuka in Hadejia during the active September 2020 flood disaster.
Floodwater covered the Ganaja axis and other roads in Lokoja and stranded motorists after the Niger overflowed its banks.
Bayelsa governor assessed flooded communities in Yenagoa and Southern Ijaw before ordering school closures.
Heavy rainfall filled drains and extended floodwater onto major Onitsha roads; traders reported floodwater entering shops.
An all-night downpour submerged large parts of Makurdi including Idye Wurukum Gyado Villa and Kucha Utebe with houses vehicles and belongings in floodwater.
Roads and residential areas across Yenagoa including Captain Ayeni Saptex Osiri Tombia Edepie Igbogene and Okutukutu were submerged and some residents left their homes.
Severe flooding affected Makurdi and multiple Benue communities in late September 2022.
Severe flooding affected Jigawa including Hadejia-area communities in September 2022.
